classification.difficultyReason: Apply explicitly named rhombus properties across three supplied marked diagrams, combine equilateral/supplementary angles and opposite-side lengths. Selection and short linked deductions are required, but the property family is directly cued and no new proof structure is invented.

content.prompt: Use the properties of a rhombus to find the values of $x$, $y$, $z$, $α$ and $β$ in the diagrams below.

spec.description: Editable native geometry preserves complete source incidences, equality/parallel/right-angle marks and all given/unknown labels. House black outlines,10pt labels; source positions are schematic, no measuring task.
spec.mathematics: All six marked intervals equal; right triangle is equilateral, left quadrilateral a rhombus. Unknown x,alpha,beta.
spec.answerVisibility: All original unknown symbols retained, no computed answer marks.

answer.worked: All marked intervals equal the given $6\text{ cm}$, so $x=6\text{ cm}$. The triangle on the right is equilateral, so its base angle is $60^\circ$. The adjacent rhombus angle is $\alpha=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ$. Adjacent rhombus angles are supplementary, so $\beta=60^\circ$.

spec.description: Editable native geometry preserves complete source incidences, equality/parallel/right-angle marks and all given/unknown labels. House black outlines,10pt labels; source positions are schematic, no measuring task.
spec.mathematics: Rhombus all sides equal; both diagonals present,30-degree half angle at lowerleft. Alpha left crossing angle, beta lower-right half angle.
spec.answerVisibility: All original unknown symbols retained, no computed answer marks.

answer.worked: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so $\alpha=90^\circ$. The diagonal bisects the lower-left angle, so that angle is $2\times30^\circ=60^\circ$. The adjacent lower-right angle is $120^\circ$, and the other diagonal bisects it, giving $\beta=60^\circ$.

spec.mathematics: Upperleft rhombus side4; both top segments equal4. Outerparallelogram parallel pairs;70degreeupperleft interior, unknowny,z,alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: All original unknown symbols retained, no computed answer marks.

answer.worked: The equality marks give both top segments length $4$, so the whole top is $4+4=8$. Opposite sides of the large parallelogram are equal, giving $z=8$. The upper-right quadrilateral is also a parallelogram, so its lower side has the length of its top side: $y=4$. The lower-left angle of the large parallelogram is $70^\circ$ by corresponding angles, so $\alpha=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ$.
